question: Which among the following National Parks is not located in Maharashtra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bandhavgarh National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's Bandhavgarh National Park **is a national park situated in **Madhya Pradesh's Umaria district**.
 
• With a land size of 105 square kilometers, Bandhavgarh was first designated as a national park in 1968 and later changed its status to Tiger Reserve in 1993. Currently, the core area is 716 square kilometers.
 
• The biodiversity of this park is very high. There are numerous types of deer and a sizable breeding population of leopards in the park.
 
• In 1951, Maharaja Martand Singh of Rewa managed to catch the first white tiger in this area. Mohan, the white tiger, is currently on display and stuffed in the Maharajas of Rewa's palace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gugamal National Park **is located in the Amravati district of Maharashtra and is known for its diverse flora and fauna, including tigers, leopards, sloth bears, and Indian bison.
 
• **Tadoba National Park **is located in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra and is famous for its tiger reserve, where tourists can go on jungle safaris to spot tigers and other wildlife.
 
• **Navegaon National Park **is located in the Gondia district of Maharashtra and is popular for its bird sanctuary, where several migratory and resident bird species can be spotted.
